The way I work

### A practical approach to complex challenges.

Product and architecture for governed enterprise AI.

- 01 Understand the context. The decision, the constraints and the people involved.
- 02 Design the right system. Product, data access, controls and architecture together.
- 03 Connect decisions to delivery. Align ownership, engineering and the operating model.
- 04 Make production governable. Evaluation, adoption and observability — not just a pilot.
I’m Vadim Vladymtsev, CTO at StackLevel Group. I work across product, architecture and engineering to help enterprise AI initiatives move from use-case selection to governed production.

Enterprise AI becomes useful only when the product, data access, controls, ownership and delivery system work together. My focus is the operating layer around the model: what the system is allowed to do, how it is evaluated, how users adopt it, and how it remains observable in production.

## About & Contact
https://vadimohka.com/about.html

About

### Vadim Vladymtsev.

Enterprise AI CTO and product operator.

Vadim Vladymtsev is CTO at StackLevel Group, focused on product, architecture and governed deployment for regulated organisations. His international focus is enterprise AI conversations with organizations in the United States and the United Arab Emirates.

How I work

### Product thinking. Engineering depth.

The work joins product choices, architecture, security context, adoption and engineering delivery. The goal is a system people can operate, review and improve in real conditions.

### Make the boundary clear

Define the use case, data access, owners and decisions before the system grows around assumptions.

### Turn uncertainty into checks

Expose the risks that change the next commitment, sequence or operating choice.

## Century AI Studio
https://vadimohka.com/century.html

Century AI Studio · Product context

### Private AI. Under your control.

Century is a product surface between AI consumers and the models, data and infrastructure underneath: chat, agents, workflows, APIs, protected data access and operational controls.

01 · Enterprise problem

### More than a model.

Enterprise AI also needs controlled access to company data, a place for users and systems to work with it, a deployment boundary, and enough logs and policy to review what happened.

### One entry point

Chat, constructors and APIs give teams a shared product surface for AI work.

### Protected context

Documents, databases and internal services can be connected within defined access boundaries.

### Operational control

Roles, policies, logs and traces make AI activity visible for operation and review.

02 · Product surface

### One platform. Connected capabilities.

### Chat and assistants

Internal chat and AI assistants for employees, customers and operational work.

### Agentic workflows

Workflow and automation modes for repeatable steps, escalation and human participation.

### Data and text-to-SQL

Document search with source links plus natural-language access to structured business data.

### API and integrations

Connections to internal databases and corporate services through APIs, queues and protected connectors.

Capability wording is based on the current Century product site and may change as the product evolves.

03 · Architecture and deployment model

### Your infrastructure. Your boundary.

The product site describes isolated instances on customer servers, on-premise, VPC and private-cloud options. It also describes local processing, policy checks before data access, and integration through protected connectors.

- 01 On-premise, VPC or private cloud
- 02 Local processing inside the controlled contour
- 03 Policy-based access to data
- 04 APIs, queues and protected connectors
How the product fits

AI consumers → Century entry point → security, data and compliance guarantees → models, data and infrastructure → protected deployment contour.

04 · Governance and observability

### Control, built in.

### Access and policies

Role-based access and policy controls are part of the described product boundary.

### Logs and audit

Requests, models, tokens and costs can be logged for operational review and audit work.

### Leak and injection protection

The product source describes protections against data leakage and prompt injection; implementation depends on the deployment context.

05 · Relationship and product context

### Product record & relationship.

Century is the product anchor for the governed-private-AI positioning on this site. Public product material describes capabilities and recognition; it does not establish Vadim's exact Century title or personal ownership, so this page does not assign one.

Century recognition

### Third place, AI Product Leader

Century received third place in the AI Product Leader category at IT-Akademgrad 2025. This is product recognition, not a personal award.

Boundary

### What this page covers.

No live adoption count, client case, roadmap promise, personal title or deployment outcome is added without a confirmed source.

06 · Product site

### Explore what comes next.

Use the Century site for the current product description and contact route. Use this page for the evidence boundary and relationship context.

## Enterprise AI
https://vadimohka.com/enterprise.html

Enterprise AI · Governed deployment

### From AI pilot to real operations.

A decision-led way to move from use-case selection to controlled production: define the boundary, make ownership explicit, and design the system that people can review and operate.

01 · Decisions

### The decisions that matter.

### Use-case selection

Choose a workflow where data, ownership, review and value can be made explicit.

### Architecture

Decide how models, retrieval, integrations, access and deployment boundaries fit together.

### Governance

Define evaluation, human review, source grounding, audit and escalation before rollout.

### Operating ownership

Make product, security, engineering and risk responsibilities visible after the pilot.

02 · Operating path

### A clear path forward.

### Frame

Clarify the decision, users, constraints, data and success conditions.

### Design

Map product scope, architecture, access boundaries, evaluation and review.

### Test

Use source-grounded scenarios and operational checks to expose risk early.

### Operate

Set ownership, observability, escalation and deployment controls for the next boundary.

This is a method for making a decision and its constraints explicit; it is not a guarantee of delivery or an implied client case.

03 · Governance and security context

### Governance by design.

The relevant questions are practical: who can access which data, how sources are grounded, when a human reviews an output, what is logged, what is observable, and which deployment model is acceptable.

- 01 Access boundaries and data handling
- 02 Source grounding and evaluation
- 03 Human review and escalation
- 04 Audit and observability
- 05 Private, on-premise or VPC deployment choices
04 · Deliverables and boundaries

### Clarity you can act on.

### Decision brief

Priority use case, constraints, stakeholders, assumptions and the decision to be made.

### Operating design

Product and architecture boundary, access model, evaluation plan and human-review path.

### Production readiness view

Open risks, ownership questions, evidence still needed and a scoped next step.

The work does not include a security certification, a promise of regulatory approval, or a named client outcome without a confirmed source.

05 · Relevant track record

### Product meets practice.

Product

### Governed private AI in one product surface.

Century's public product material describes private/on-premise/VPC deployment, local processing, audit/logging and integrations. This is company-level product material, not a personal client case.

Published · 2 March 2026

### Why enterprise AI pilots stall.

Vadim authored a Vaiti article on “pilot hell” and the move from pilots toward production, a relevant public insight for executives assessing operating readiness.

06 · Next action

### Let’s define the next step.

Share the organisation type, current decision, constraints, timeline and stakeholders. Keep confidential data out of the first message; the first step is to define the decision boundary.

Enterprise AI strategy and architecture inquiries from organizations in the United States and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are welcome.

## AI Technical Due Diligence
https://vadimohka.com/investors.html

Technical assessment · AI companies

AI Technical Due Diligence.

### Clarity before commitment.

A practical assessment of whether an AI product, its data, architecture, team and deployment claims can survive real operating conditions.

### Product. Data. Architecture.

### What holds up. What remains open.

Evidence before the next commitment.

01 · Decision

### Look beyond the demo.

The assessment asks whether the product solves a real workflow, whether the data position is defensible, whether the architecture and team can support the claims, and what remains unproven before a decision.

### Product reality

What exists beyond the demo, and which workflow is actually supported?

### Data and models

Are data rights, feedback loops, model choices and RAG quality clear?

### Architecture

Can integrations, security, governance and observability survive deployment?

### Team execution

Can the team make trade-offs, expose technical debt and ship the next boundary?

02 · Assessment dimensions

### Ask the harder questions.

### Deployment readiness

What changes when the product enters a customer's real environment?

### Economics and observability

What is measured, what is expensive, and what can the team see in operation?

### Open questions

Which product, data, security or delivery statements still need evidence?

Examples here are assessment questions. They are not claims about a completed review, a portfolio or a transaction.

03 · Process

### A focused review.

- 01 Management and technical interviews
- 02 Architecture and repository review when permitted
- 03 Product material and deployment-context review
- 04 Risk register with red flags and open questions
- 05 Written technical memo and decision briefing
04 · Deliverables

### Evidence. Not assumptions.

### Review summary

What was looked at, what was supplied, and which questions remain open.

### Technical memo

Architecture, data, deployment, observability, team execution and hidden technical debt.

### Decision briefing

Red flags, open questions, limitations and the next technical checks to run.

05 · Boundaries

### A technical view. A better-informed decision.

This work is a technical assessment of product, data, architecture, deployment and team claims. It is not legal, financial, accounting or regulated investment advice, and it does not allocate capital, recommend a transaction or guarantee an outcome.

AI technical due diligence inquiries from investors and investment teams in the United States and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are welcome.

## CTO Advisory
https://vadimohka.com/founders.html

Founder support · CTO-level diagnosis

### Product. Architecture. Aligned.

A practical diagnostic for founders who need to identify the real constraint, make ownership explicit and choose a credible next operating plan.

01 · Trigger conditions

### Find the real constraint.

### Roadmap and architecture diverge

Product commitments depend on technical decisions nobody has made explicit.

### Busy does not mean predictable

The team is active, but delivery, ownership and review remain unclear.

### Pilot work cannot become a product

AI scope is larger than the evidence, workflow or operating model can support.

### Commercial commitments are blocked

Engineering risks, integration questions or unclear ownership make the next promise unsafe.

### Decisions keep reopening

Architecture, product and team trade-offs are revisited without a shared decision map.

### The next boundary is unclear

There is no agreed sequence for what to fix, test, defer or own next.

02 · Diagnostic process

### Turn complexity into a plan.

- 01 Clarify the product decision and operating constraint
- 02 Review product scope, architecture, information and ownership
- 03 Prioritise risks by consequence and reversibility
- 04 Agree the next cadence, decision owners and checks
03 · Deliverables

### A direction. And a next step.

### Decision map

What must be decided, by whom, with which evidence and constraints.

### Product/architecture diagnosis

Where product scope, system design and engineering reality have separated.

### Prioritised technical risks

The few risks that change the next commitment, sequence or ownership.

### 30/60/90-day operating plan

A sequenced plan for decisions, ownership, review cadence and optional architecture work.

04 · Builder context

### Grounded in the work.

Product

### From product surface to operating boundary.

Century is the product anchor for governed private enterprise AI. Its public product site provides company-level product context; it is not presented here as a personal client outcome.

BSUIR background

### Teaching and programming systems.

Official BSUIR records support specific teaching, coaching and competition-organisation context. These records show an engineering foundation, not a commercial outcome.

05 · Boundaries

### Start with a CTO diagnostic.

The work focuses on product, architecture, engineering ownership and delivery decisions. It does not include fundraising advice, introductions, investment advice, exit planning or a promise of growth. Testimonials and commercial outcomes are shared only when separately approved and evidenced.

CTO advisory inquiries from founders and executive teams in the United States and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are welcome.

03 · Bio variants

### A few words about Vadim.

Vadim Vladymtsev is CTO at StackLevel Group, focused on enterprise AI product, architecture and governed deployment for regulated organisations.

Vadim Vladymtsev is CTO at StackLevel Group and an enterprise AI product operator. His work connects product design, architecture, governed data access, engineering delivery and operational control, with a focus on helping regulated organisations move priority AI use cases beyond pilot stage.

Vadim Vladymtsev is CTO at StackLevel Group and an enterprise AI product operator focused on governed private AI for regulated organisations. He works across product, architecture and engineering, with attention to data access, source grounding, observability, deployment control and user adoption. His earlier career includes software engineering, university teaching and competitive-programming coaching at BSUIR. His public work covers enterprise AI adoption, emerging AI operating roles, technical diligence and the practical constraints that prevent pilots from becoming production systems.

Speaker introduction: Vadim Vladymtsev is CTO at StackLevel Group. He speaks about enterprise AI deployment, governance, product architecture, technical diligence and the organisational conditions required to move from pilot to production.
